name: Markup.Atoms
comment:
Accessible atom constructors — the v1 cross-library atom vocabulary.

Every function here produces an `Element` carrying a `Markup.Kind.Shared` marker
in a specific role-tier field, admissible wherever the corresponding slot kind is
declared open (`shared:text`, `shared:link`, `shared:label`, `shared:icon`).

## Design principles (tesk9/accessible-html-informed)

  - **`link`** requires `href` AND at least one discernible text child. A link
    with no text content is a WCAG 2.4.4 failure; the type system makes it
    unrepresentable by requiring a mandatory first child
    (`Element { text : Markup.Kind.Shared } msg`) plus an optional rest list.
    The mandatory-first-child pattern is the standard Elm idiom for enforcing
    non-empty collections at the type level.

  - **`label`** carries the `label` atom role and accepts text and icon children
    (closed slot `{ text : Shared, icon : Shared }`). Because atom producers use
    OPEN rows (`{ s | text : Shared }`), both text atoms and icon atoms satisfy
    the closed slot via row unification — Elm instantiates the open `s` to the
    remaining field. This means text-only labels, icon-only labels, and
    text+icon labels all type-check, while arbitrary non-atom content is
    rejected. The `for` association is an optional `String`; when supplied the
    generator stamps `for="<id>"` on the produced `<label>` element. When
    omitted, the label wraps its control (implicit association).

  - **`icon`** must be EITHER aria-hidden decorative (`iconDecorative`) OR carry
    a discernible label (`iconLabeled`). There is no silently-unlabeled
    constructor — the two constructors enforce the WCAG 1.1.1 choice by
    construction.

## Deferred atoms (v2)

  - **`heading`**: deferred — requires a level decision (typed enum vs. 6 separate
    constructors). Not in v1.
  - **`image`**: deferred — requires `Alt = Informative String | Decorative`
    (plan correction 6) to enforce alt-text by construction. Not in v1.

## Icon note

`iconDecorative` and `iconLabeled` produce elements carrying the `icon` atom role.
Icons are represented as raw `Html msg` because there is no single HTML element for
"icon" — they are typically inline SVG or font glyphs. The constructors wrap the
raw SVG in the appropriate ARIA annotations and return a typed `Element`.

@docs text, link, label
@docs iconDecorative, iconLabeled

values.name: iconDecorative
values.comment:
Decorative icon — aria-hidden, invisible to assistive technology.

Use when the icon is purely visual and an adjacent text label provides the
accessible name. The `aria-hidden="true"` attribute is stamped automatically,
satisfying WCAG 1.1.1 for decorative images.

    -- Icon + adjacent text label (the text IS the accessible name)
    Markup.Atoms.iconDecorative svgContent
values.type: Html.Html msg -> Markup.Element.Element { s | icon : Markup.Kind.Shared } msg

values.name: iconLabeled
values.comment:
Labeled icon — carries an `aria-label` visible to assistive technology.

Use when the icon IS the accessible content and there is no adjacent text label.
The `label` string becomes the accessible name via `aria-label`, satisfying WCAG
1.1.1 for informative images.

    -- Standalone icon button — the label IS the accessible name
    Markup.Atoms.iconLabeled { label = "Close dialog" } svgContent

**Known limitation:** an empty-string `label = ""` compiles but produces an
inaccessible icon (empty `aria-label` is equivalent to no label). This cannot be
prevented at the type level without a custom non-empty-string type. It is a
candidate for an elm-review rule (`NoEmptyAriaLabel` or similar) to catch at
lint time.
values.type: { label : String.String } -> Html.Html msg -> Markup.Element.Element { s | icon : Markup.Kind.Shared } msg

values.name: label
values.comment:
Form label atom. Carries the `label` role-tier marker.

Accepts text and icon children via the closed slot `{ text : Shared, icon :
Shared }`. Because atom producers use OPEN rows (`{ s | text : Shared }`), both
text atoms and icon atoms satisfy this slot via row unification — text-only,
icon-only, and text+icon labels all type-check, while arbitrary non-atom content
is rejected.

Pass `for = Just "control-id"` for explicit label↔control association (WCAG 1.3.1).
Pass `for = Nothing` when the label wraps its control implicitly.

    -- Explicit association with text
    Markup.Atoms.label { for = Just "email-input" }
        [ Markup.Atoms.text "Email address" ]

    -- Text + icon label
    Markup.Atoms.label { for = Just "search-input" }
        [ Markup.Atoms.iconDecorative svgSearch
        , Markup.Atoms.text "Search"
        ]

    -- Implicit (label wraps control)
    Markup.Atoms.label { for = Nothing }
        [ Markup.Atoms.text "Email" ]

Decision (CF-12 / FIX 3): widened from text-only to text+icon to match the
`slots.json` declaration (`["shared:text", "shared:icon"]`) and cover the common
accessible pattern of icon+text labels. slots.json and Atoms.label now agree.
values.type: { for : Maybe.Maybe String.String } -> List.List (Markup.Element.Element { text : Markup.Kind.Shared, icon : Markup.Kind.Shared } msg) -> Markup.Element.Element { s | label : Markup.Kind.Shared } msg

values.name: link
values.comment:
Accessible hyperlink atom. Requires `href`, a mandatory first discernible
text child, and an optional rest list of additional text children.

    Markup.Atoms.link { href = "/home" }
        (Markup.Atoms.text "Home")
        []

The mandatory-first-child pattern (`first` + `rest`) enforces at the type level
that a link always has at least one discernible text child, satisfying WCAG 2.4.4
(Link Purpose). The old `link {href} []` call pattern no longer type-checks — you
must supply a first child.

The closed child row `{ text : Markup.Kind.Shared }` ensures the link's
discernible content is typed: you must pass text-atom children, not arbitrary
content.
values.type: { href : String.String } -> Markup.Element.Element { text : Markup.Kind.Shared } msg -> List.List (Markup.Element.Element { text : Markup.Kind.Shared } msg) -> Markup.Element.Element { s | link : Markup.Kind.Shared } msg

values.name: text
values.comment:
Inline text atom — wraps a plain `String` in a `<span>` carrying the `text`
role-tier marker. Use wherever a `{ s | text : Markup.Kind.Shared }` slot is
expected.

    Markup.Atoms.text "Save"
values.type: String.String -> Markup.Element.Element { s | text : Markup.Kind.Shared } msg

name: Markup.Attributes
comment:

setters are independent of the phantom slot/capability rows: each carries a fully
open `capability` row and therefore type-checks inside any component's attribute
list (`Markup.<Component>.view [ Markup.Attributes.id "…" ] …`).

They mirror the universal-attribute precedent set by `Markup.Aria`: pure HTML truth,
no CEM data. The barrel (`Markup`) re-exposes them flat as `Markup.id`, `Markup.for`,
`Markup.class`, `Markup.style`.

name: Markup.Element
comment:
A phantom-typed wrapper around a lazy [`Node`](Markup-Node): an `Element supported msg`
is a piece of renderable content whose `supported` row records which slot kinds
it is allowed to occupy. Generated component `view` functions produce and consume
`Element`s; the row is what lets the compiler reject content in a slot a component
does not admit.

The type is **opaque** and the raw-to-phantom constructor (`fromNode`) is _not_
re-exported here — it lives in [`Markup.Element.Internal`](Markup-Element-Internal),
reachable only by generated `Markup.*` code and a team's `Seam` module.
The safe out-bound extraction [`toNode`](#toNode), slot tagging, and `map` remain
public. There is no library-defined `text` constructor: text/link/label are
config-declared userland **seams**, crafted in the team's `Seam`
module on the generated `Markup.Seam` contracts.

name: Markup.Html.Attr
comment:
A capability-typed attribute: a deferred `Html.Attribute` (thunked so it can
be carried through the typed layers without being applied) tagged with a
`capability` row recording which attribute a binding site admits. The generated
setters produce `Attr`s with a specific capability.

The type is **opaque** and the two free capability assertions — `attribute`
(mint at any row) and `forget` (erase the row) — are _not_ re-exported here; they
live in [`Markup.Html.Attr.Internal`](Markup-Cem-Attr-Internal), reachable only by
generated `Markup.*` code and a team's `Seam` module. The extraction
[`toAttribute`](#toAttribute) and the typed [`slot`](#slot) constructor stay
public.

@docs Attr

name: Markup.Kind
comment:
The kind vocabulary for the Markup runtime.

Two distinct types live here:

  - `Shared` — the cross-library atom marker. An `Element` carrying
    `Shared` in a kind field is admissible wherever the corresponding
    slot kind opts in (`shared:text`, `shared:link`, etc.), regardless
    of which library produced that element.

  - `Brand` — Markup's own private brand. Elements produced by
    Markup structural HTML elements (div, nav, section, etc.) carry
    this brand. Slots typed with a private kind reject elements from
    other libraries (nominal brand segregation, zero runtime cost).

@docs Shared, Brand

unions.name: Brand
unions.comment:
The per-library phantom kind marker for Markup's private-tier
elements. Never constructed by user code.

unions.name: Shared
unions.comment:
The cross-library atom marker. Marks an `Element` as carrying a
shared atom role (text, link, label, icon, …). Content typed as
`Shared` is admissible wherever the corresponding slot kind is accepted
by any library that opts in to that atom role.

name: Markup.Node
comment:
The lazy intermediate representation every `Element` is built from: a `Node`
is either a component (a partially-applied bottom-layer render function plus its
attributes and children), a text leaf, or an escape hatch holding raw `Html`.
Keeping construction lazy lets the typed layers above rearrange and re-slot
content before anything is rendered; [`toHtml`](#toHtml) collapses it to `Html`.

The type is **opaque** and the raw-`Html` constructor (`raw`) is _not_
re-exported here — both live in [`Markup.Node.Internal`](Markup-Node-Internal),
reachable only by generated `Markup.*` code and a team's `Seam` module. The typed
builders, the extraction [`toHtml`](#toHtml), and `map` stay public.

@docs Node
@docs fromComponent, addAttr, addChild, text, toHtml, map

name: Markup.Token.Core
comment:
The primitive behind every token enum. A `Value tags` is a string tagged
with a phantom `tags` row naming which token families it belongs to, so a token
can only be passed where that family is accepted. `Supported` is the marker
written into a row to mean "this member is admitted here".

The type is **opaque** and the free constructor `token` (mint at any row) is
_not_ re-exported here — both live in
[`Markup.Token.Core.Internal`](Markup-Value-Core-Internal), reachable only by generated
`Markup.*` code and a team's `Seam` module. The extraction
[`toString`](#toString) stays public.

@docs Value, Supported
@docs toString

[`Markup.Token.Core.Internal`](Markup-Value-Core-Internal).

A phantom-tagged string token, opaque and re-exported from
